title: Build It × IQ
summary: How a multi-store marketplace connects to per-store IQ Retail APIs — from onboard and catalogue unify through Ozow pending to sales-order write and capture.

problem.headline: The problem
problem.lede: One marketplace cart. Many independent IQ worlds. Stock truth, product codes, and sales still live in each store.

blocks.label: Tension
blocks.title: One cart, many IQs
blocks.body: Shoppers need one catalogue, one checkout (Ozow), and fulfilment from the best local store. Truth for stock, price, and sales still lives in each store’s IQ Retail / IQ Enterprise system.
bullets: Each store is a standalone IQ server + database. No shared product codes across stores (cement can be 0101 in one store and CEM in another).
Store owners control their own data. There is no single group catalogue to lean on.
On-hand quantities are unreliable (stock can go negative when goods arrive on delivery note before invoice).
Paid web orders must land in IQ without re-keying, with payment and web references visible to staff.

blocks.label: What we cannot afford
blocks.title: Failure modes
bullets: Oversell from bad live quantities on the site.
Orders stuck outside IQ.
Till or network load from chatty sync.
Two stores, two SKU languages, one confused shopper.

blocks.label: Today’s reality
blocks.title: How IQ is set up
bullets: One integration endpoint per store.
IQ exposes a REST API (JSON or XML) via IQEntAPIRestServer on the store server.
API config is per store: port, SSL/TLS certificates, authentication, rate limits.
Versions can differ between stores. API behaviour depends on version alignment.

blocks.label: Catalogue reality
blocks.title: Same product, different codes
bullets: No enforced SKU scheme across stores.
Departments are more standardised than codes.
Weights, dimensions, and images are often empty.
FTG already maintains a large supplier master map that can seed unification.

solving.headline: What we are solving
solving.lede: The marketplace needs reliable reads from each store, safe writes back into IQ, and one product language for shoppers.

blocks.label: Must read
blocks.title: Per-store truth
bullets: Products / stock master (codes, departments, barcodes).
Stock signal for allocation (honest scarcity, not fragile live on-hand).
Selling prices and active promotions.

blocks.label: Must write
blocks.title: No re-key path
bullets: Sales order for paid web orders in the winning store’s IQ.
Customer create / match without duplicates.
Web order id + Ozow payment reference visible to staff.
Delivery fee line as stores already capture at POS.

blocks.label: Also required
blocks.title: Unify products across stores
blocks.body: Shoppers see one cement bag. Behind the scenes, Platform45 maps each store’s local SKU into a canonical product, using supplier master data and a confidence-scored matching engine.

solution.headline: Our solution
solution.lede: Per-store IQ REST API, Platform45 background jobs, and a matching engine in the middle. No store-side SQL agent.

blocks.label: Approach
blocks.title: API first
blocks.body: Each store runs IQEntAPIRestServer. Platform45 stores that store’s config (host, port, TLS certificates, Basic auth, rate limits). Background jobs fetch catalogue and stock, and confirm pending orders by calling the store API. A matching engine unifies divergent SKUs into one ecommerce catalogue.

blocks.label: 1 · Connect
blocks.title: Per-store API config
bullets: Listen port and IP
TLS certificate, key, password
Basic authentication
Token expiry and rate limit

blocks.label: 2 · Unify
blocks.title: Matching engine
bullets: Seed from FTG master mapping
Score by confidence
Auto-approve high confidence
Human review below the threshold
Rules learn from confirmed matches

blocks.label: 3 · Trade safely
blocks.title: Jobs + pending pay
bullets: Sync catalogue and stock in the background
No live on-hand on the front end
Checkout creates a pending order after Ozow
Job confirms with the store API, then captures

blocks.label: Stock honesty
blocks.title: Cache, don’t live-stream
blocks.body: On-hand can go negative in IQ. We prefer a cached stock signal on the storefront and a final stock check against the API only at purchase time.

blocks.label: If the API path struggles
blocks.title: File fallback
blocks.body: Scheduled stock and price exports, plus importable order files, keep a pilot alive while the REST path is hardened. Same catalogue mapping either way.
